## Every job takes energy

Making a protein, moving materials and dividing all take energy. **Mitochondria** supply the energy for most of these activities, so they are often called the powerhouses of the cell. One of them is called a **mitochondrion**.

<!-- STEP -->
## Two membranes

Each mitochondrion is surrounded by two membranes. The **outer membrane** is smooth and porous. The **inner membrane** is folded into finger-like projections called **cristae**.

<!-- STEP -->
## Why fold a membrane?

The folds increase the surface area for chemical reactions, and that helps energy production. Drag the **Folds** slider: the mitochondrion stays the same size while its inner membrane grows longer.

**Folding fits more surface into the same small space.** In the same way, many small mitochondria have more surface in total than one giant one of the same volume.

<!-- STEP -->
## From glucose to ATP

In mitochondria, glucose and other molecules are broken down to release energy. This process is **cellular respiration**. The energy released is stored in a molecule called **ATP** (Adenosine Triphosphate), and the cell uses ATP for most of its activities. That is why ATP is called the energy currency.
